questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The atmosphere is heated more by incoming solar radiation than by terrestrial radiation.
Statement-II: Carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases in the atmosphere are good absorbers of long wave radiation.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Most sunlight passes through the air and heats the ground; the air is heated mainly by long-wave terrestrial radiation absorbed by greenhouse gases. So Statement-I is wrong and Statement-II right.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q1

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Thickness of the troposphere at the equator is much greater as compared to poles.
Statement-II: At the equator, heat is transported to great heights by strong convectional currents.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The troposphere is about 18 km thick at the equator and 8 km at the poles because strong convection carries heat high at the equator. Statement-II explains Statement-I.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q2

questions.q:
Consider the following:
1. Pyroclastic debris
2. Ash and dust
3. Nitrogen compounds
4. Sulphur compounds
How many of the above are products of volcanic eruptions?
questions.e: Eruptions throw out pyroclastic debris, ash and dust, and gases including nitrogen and sulphur compounds. All four.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q3

questions.q:
Which of the following is/are correct inference/inferences from isothermal maps in the month of January?
1. The isotherms deviate to the north over the ocean and to the south over the continent.
2. The presence of cold ocean currents, Gulf Stream and North Atlantic Drift make the North Atlantic Ocean colder and the isotherms bend towards the north.
Select the answer using the code given below:
questions.e: In January isotherms bend north over the warmer oceans and south over colder continents. The Gulf Stream and North Atlantic Drift are warm currents, so 2 is wrong.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q4

questions.q: Which of the following countries are well known as the two largest cocoa producers in the world?
questions.e: Côte d'Ivoire and Ghana on the Gulf of Guinea are the two largest cocoa producers.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q5

questions.q: With reference to the Himalayan rivers joining the Ganga downstream of Prayagraj from West to East, which one of the following sequences is correct?
questions.e: Downstream of Prayagraj the Gomati joins first, then the Ghaghara, the Gandak and finally the Kosi.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q6

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Rainfall is one of the reasons for weathering of rocks.
Statement-II: Rain water contains carbon dioxide in solution.
Statement-III: Rain water contains atmospheric oxygen.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-II and Statement-III are correct and both of them explain Statement-I
Both Statement-II and Statement-III are correct, but only one of them explains Statement-I
Only one of the Statements II and III is correct and that explains Statement-I
Neither Statement-II nor Statement-III is correct
questions.e: Rain dissolves CO₂ (forming a weak acid) and oxygen (which oxidises minerals); both drive chemical weathering. Both explain Statement-I.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q7

questions.q:
Consider the following countries:
1. Finland
2. Germany
3. Norway
4. Russia
How many of the above countries have a border with the North Sea?
questions.e: Germany and Norway border the North Sea. Finland and Russia face the Baltic.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q8

questions.q:
Consider the following information: Waterfall Region River
1. Dhuandhar Malwa Narmada
2. Hundru Chota Nagpur Subarnarekha
3. Gersoppa Western Ghats Netravati In how many of the above rows is the given information correctly matched?
questions.e: Hundru Falls is on the Subarnarekha in Chota Nagpur. Dhuandhar is near Jabalpur, not Malwa, and Jog (Gersoppa) is on the Sharavati.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q9

questions.q:
Consider the following information: Region Name of the mountain range Type of mountain
1. Central Asia Vosges Fold mountain
2. Europe Alps Block mountain
3. North America Appalachians Fold mountain
4. South America Andes Fold mountain In how many of the above rows is the given information correctly matched?
questions.e: The Appalachians and Andes are fold mountains. The Vosges are in Europe and are block mountains, and the Alps are fold mountains.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q10

questions.q:
Consider the following airports:
1. Donyi Polo Airport
2. Kushinagar International Airport
3. Vijayawada International Airport In the recent past, which of the above have been constructed as Greenfield projects?
questions.e: Donyi Polo (Itanagar) and Kushinagar are greenfield airports. Vijayawada is an older airport at Gannavaram.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q11

questions.q:
With reference to "water vapour", which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. It is a gas, the amount of which decreases with altitude.
2. Its percentage is maximum at the poles.
Select the answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Water vapour decreases with altitude. It is highest in the warm, humid tropics, not at the poles.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q12

questions.q:
Consider the following description:
1. Annual and daily range of temperatures is low.
2. Precipitation occurs throughout the year.
3. Precipitation varies between 50 cm – 250 cm.
What is this type of climate?
questions.e: Small temperature ranges, rain all year and 50-250 cm of precipitation describe the Marine West Coast climate.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q13

questions.q:
With reference to "Coriolis force", which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. It increases with increase in wind velocity.
2. It is maximum at the poles and is absent at the equator.
Select the answer using the code given below:
questions.e: The Coriolis force increases with wind speed and latitude: maximum at the poles, zero at the equator.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q14

questions.q:
On June 21 every year, which of the following latitude(s) experience(s) a sunlight of more than 12 hours?
1. Equator
2. Tropic of Cancer
3. Tropic of Capricorn
4. Arctic Circle
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: On 21 June all places north of the equator get more than 12 hours of daylight; the equator gets 12. So the Tropic of Cancer and the Arctic Circle.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q15

questions.q: One of the following regions has the world's largest tropical peatland, which holds about three years worth of global carbon emissions from fossil fuels; and the possible destruction of which can exert detrimental effect on the global climate. Which one of the following denotes that region?
questions.e: The Cuvette Centrale peatlands of the Congo Basin are the world's largest tropical peatland, holding about three years' worth of global emissions.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q16

questions.q:
With reference to perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) that are used in making many consumer products, consider the following statements:
1. PFAS are found to be widespread in drinking water, food and food packaging materials.
2. PFAS are not easily degraded in the environment.
3. Persistent exposure to PFAS can lead to bioaccumulation in animal bodies.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: PFAS 'forever chemicals' are widespread in water, food and packaging, resist degradation, and bioaccumulate. All three are correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q17
questions.u: Solid Waste, Hazardous Chemicals & Heavy Metals

questions.q:
Consider the following:
1. Carabid beetles
2. Centipedes
3. Flies
4. Termites
5. Wasps Parasitoid species are found in how many of the above kind of organisms?
questions.e: Parasitoids are found among wasps, flies and some beetles such as carabids. Centipedes and termites are not parasitoids.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q18

questions.q:
Consider the following plants:
1. Groundnut
2. Horse-gram
3. Soybean
How many of the above belong to the pea family?
questions.e: Groundnut, horse-gram and soybean are all legumes of the pea family (Fabaceae).
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q19

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The Indian Flying Fox is placed under the "vermin" category in the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972.
Statement-II: The Indian Flying Fox feeds on the blood of other animals.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: UPSC dropped this question. The Indian flying fox is a fruit bat, not a blood-feeder, and the 2022 amendment removed the vermin schedule.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q20

questions.q: The organisms "Cicada, Froghopper and Pond skater" are:
questions.e: Cicadas, froghoppers and pond skaters are all insects (true bugs, Hemiptera).
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q21

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Many chewing gums found in the market are considered a source of environmental pollution.
Statement-II: Many chewing gums contain plastic as gum base.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Most chewing gum uses a synthetic plastic gum base that does not biodegrade, which is why discarded gum pollutes. Statement-II explains Statement-I.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q22
questions.u: Solid Waste, Hazardous Chemicals & Heavy Metals

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs: Country Animal found in its natural habitat
1. Brazil Indri
2. Indonesia Elk
3. Madagascar Bonobo
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: The indri lives only in Madagascar, the bonobo in DR Congo and the elk in North America and northern Asia. None is correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q23

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding World Toilet Organization:
1. It is one of the agencies of the United Nations.
2. World Toilet Summit, World Toilet Day and World Toilet College are the initiatives of this organization, to inspire action to tackle the global sanitation crisis.
3. The main focus of its function is to grant funds to the least developed countries and developing countries to achieve the end of open defecation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The World Toilet Organization is a Singapore-based NGO, not a UN agency. It started World Toilet Day, the Summit and the College, and works through advocacy, not grants.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q24

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Lions do not have a particular breeding season.
2. Unlike most other big cats, cheetahs do not roar.
3. Unlike male lions, male leopards do not proclaim their territory by scent marking.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Lions breed year-round and cheetahs cannot roar. Male leopards do scent-mark their territories, so 3 is wrong.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q25

questions.q: Which one of the following is the correct description of "100 Million Farmers"?
o: It is a platform for accelerating the transition towards food and water systems that are net-zero (carbon), nature-positive and that aims to increase farmer resilience.
It is an international alliance and a network of individuals and farming organisations interested in supporting and strengthening the development of the organic animal husbandry.
It is a digital platform fully integrated with service providers and built on blockchain that lets buyers, sellers and third parties trade fertilizers quickly and securely.

It is a platform with the mission of encouraging the farmers to form Farmer Product Organisations or Agribusiness Consortiums, thus facilitating the access to global open markets to sell their products.
questions.e: 100 Million Farmers is a platform to move food and water systems towards net-zero, nature-positive models while making farmers more resilient.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q26

questions.q:
Consider the following:
1. Battery storage
2. Biomass generators
3. Fuel cells
4. Rooftop solar photovoltaic units
How many of the above are considered "Distributed Energy Resources"?
questions.e: Distributed energy resources are small units near the point of use: batteries, biomass generators, fuel cells and rooftop solar. All four.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q27

questions.q: Which one of the following shows a unique relationship with an insect that has coevolved with it and that is the only insect that can pollinate this tree?
questions.e: Fig trees and fig wasps have coevolved; each fig species is pollinated only by its partner wasp.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q28

questions.q:
Consider the following:
1. Butterflies
2. Fish
3. Frogs
How many of the above have poisonous species among them?
questions.e: Monarch butterflies, pufferfish and poison dart frogs are examples of poisonous species in each group.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q29

questions.q:
Consider the following:
1. Cashew
2. Papaya
3. Red sanders
How many of the above trees are actually native to India?
questions.e: Only red sanders is native to India (Eastern Ghats). Cashew and papaya came from the Americas.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q30

questions.q:
With reference to radioisotope thermoelectric generators (RTGs), consider the following statements:
1. RTGs are miniature fission reactors.
2. RTGs are used for powering the onboard systems of spacecrafts.
3. RTGs can use Plutonium-238, which is a by-product of weapons development.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: RTGs convert heat from the natural decay of plutonium-238 into electricity for spacecraft. They are not fission reactors.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q31

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Giant stars live much longer than dwarf stars.
Statement-II: Compared to dwarf stars, giant stars have a greater rate of nuclear reactions.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Giant stars burn fuel at much higher rates, so they live much shorter lives than dwarf stars. Statement-I is wrong; II is right.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q32

questions.q: Which one of the following is synthesised in human body that dilates blood vessels and increases blood flow?
questions.e: Nitric oxide made in blood vessel linings relaxes the muscle and widens the vessels.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q33

questions.q:
Consider the following activities:
1. Identification of narcotics on passengers at airports or in aircraft
2. Monitoring of precipitation
3. Tracking the migration of animals In how many of the above activities can the radars be used?
questions.e: Radar can monitor precipitation and track migrating animals, but it cannot detect narcotics on people.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q34

questions.q:
Consider the following aircraft:
1. Rafael
2. MiG-29
3. Tejas MK-1
How many of the above are considered fifth generation fighter aircraft?
questions.e: Rafale, MiG-29 and Tejas Mk-1 are 4th or 4.5 generation fighters; none is fifth generation.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q35

questions.q:
In which of the following are hydrogels used?
1. Controlled drug delivery in patients
2. Mobile air-conditioning systems
3. Preparation of industrial lubricants
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Hydrogels are mainly used in medicine, such as controlled drug delivery. They are not used in car air-conditioning or industrial lubricants.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q36

questions.q: Which one of the following is the exhaust pipe emission from Fuel Cell Electric Vehicles, powered by hydrogen?
questions.e: A hydrogen fuel cell combines hydrogen and oxygen; the only exhaust is water vapour.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q37

questions.q: Recently, the term "pumped-storage hydropower" is actually and appropriately discussed in the context of which one of the following?
questions.e: Pumped-storage hydropower stores energy by pumping water uphill when power is cheap and releasing it through turbines at peak times.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q38

questions.q: "Membrane Bioreactors" are often discussed in the context of:
questions.e: Membrane bioreactors combine biological treatment with membrane filtration to clean wastewater.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q39

questions.q: With reference to the Indian economy, “Collateral Borrowing and Lending Obligations” are the instruments of:
questions.e: CBLO is a money market instrument for short-term collateralised borrowing and lending.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q40

questions.q: The total fertility rate in an economy is defined as:
o: the number of children born per 1000 people in the population in a year.
the number of children born to a couple in their lifetime in a given population.
the birth rate minus death rate.
the average number of live births a woman would have by the end of her child-bearing age.
questions.e: TFR is the average number of children a woman would have over her child-bearing years.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q41

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In India, Non-Banking Financial Companies can access the Liquidity Adjustment Facility window of the Reserve Bank of India.
2. In India, Foreign Institutional Investors can hold the Government Securities (G-Secs).
3. In India, Stock Exchanges can offer separate trading platforms for debts.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Standalone primary dealers (NBFCs) can use the LAF, foreign investors can hold G-Secs within limits, and exchanges can run debt platforms. All three are correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q42

questions.q:
In India, which of the following can trade in Corporate Bonds and Government Securities?
1. Insurance Companies
2. Pension Funds
3. Retail Investors
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Insurers, pension funds and retail investors can all trade corporate bonds and G-Secs; retail investors use RBI Retail Direct and exchange platforms.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q43

questions.q:
Consider the following:
1. Exchange-Traded Funds (ETF)
2. Motor vehicles
3. Currency swap
Which of the above is/are considered financial instruments?
questions.e: ETFs and currency swaps are financial instruments. A motor vehicle is a physical good.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q44

questions.q:
With reference to the sectors of the Indian economy, consider the following pairs: Economic activity Sector
1. Storage of agricultural produce Secondary
2. Dairy farm Primary
3. Mineral exploration Tertiary
4. Weaving cloth Secondary
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Dairy farming is primary and weaving secondary. Storage is a tertiary service and mineral exploration belongs to the primary sector.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q45

questions.q:
Consider the following materials:
1. Agricultural residues
2. Corn grain
3. Wastewater treatment sludge
4. Wood mill waste
Which of the above can be used as feedstock for producing Sustainable Aviation Fuel?
questions.e: Sustainable aviation fuel can be made from crop residues, corn grain, wastewater sludge and wood mill waste. All four.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q46

questions.q:
With reference to physical capital in Indian economy, consider the following pairs: Items Category
1. Farmer's plough Working capital
2. Computer Fixed capital
3. Yarn used by the weaver Fixed capital
4. Petrol Working capital
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: A computer is fixed capital and petrol is working capital. A plough is fixed capital and yarn is working capital.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q47

questions.q: Which one of the following words/phrases is most appropriately used to denote "an interoperable network of 3D virtual worlds that can be accessed simultaneously by millions of users, who can exert property rights over virtual items"?
questions.e: A network of interoperable 3D virtual worlds with ownership of virtual items describes the metaverse.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q48

questions.q:
With reference to the rule/rules imposed by the Reserve Bank of India while treating foreign banks, consider the following statements:
1. There is no minimum capital requirement for wholly owned banking subsidiaries in India.
2. For wholly owned banking subsidiaries in India, at least 50% of the board members should be Indian nationals.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Foreign bank subsidiaries need a minimum capital of ₹500 crore, and the board rule counts Indians, NRIs and PIOs together. Neither statement is correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q49

questions.q:
With reference to Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) rules in India, consider the following statements:
1. CSR rules specify that expenditures that benefit the company directly or its employees will not be considered as CSR activities.
2. CSR rules do not specify minimum spending on CSR activities.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: CSR rules exclude activities that benefit the company or its employees. Section 135 requires eligible companies to spend at least 2% of profits, so 2 is wrong.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q50

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: If the United States of America (USA) were to default on its debt, holders of US Treasury Bonds will not be able to exercise their claims to receive payment.
Statement-II: The USA Government debt is not backed by any hard assets, but only by the faith of the Government.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: US government debt is backed only by the government's credit, not hard assets, which is why a default would leave holders unable to enforce payment. UPSC's key takes Statement-II as explaining Statement-I.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q51

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Syndicated lending spreads the risk of borrower default across multiple lenders.
Statement-II: The syndicated loan can be a fixed amount/lump sum of funds, but cannot be a credit line.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: UPSC dropped this question. Syndicated loans spread default risk across lenders and can be term loans or credit lines.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q52

questions.q:
Consider the following statements in respect of the digital rupee:
1. It is a sovereign currency issued by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) in alignment with its monetary policy.
2. It appears as a liability on the RBI's balance sheet.
3. It is insured against inflation by its very design.
4. It is freely convertible against commercial bank money and cash.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The digital rupee is sovereign currency issued under monetary policy, an RBI liability, and convertible with bank money and cash. It is not inflation-protected.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q53

questions.q:
With reference to ancient India, Gautama Buddha was generally known by which of the following epithets?
1. Nayaputta
2. Shakyamuni
3. Tathagata
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: None of the above are epithets of Gautama Buddha
questions.e: Shakyamuni and Tathagata are titles of the Buddha. Nayaputta (Nataputta) refers to Mahavira.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q54

questions.q:
Consider the following information: Archaeological Site State Description
1. Chandraketugarh Odisha Trading Port town
2. Inamgaon Maharashtra Chalcolithic site
3. Mangadu Kerala Megalithic site
4. Salihundam Andhra Pradesh Rock-cut cave shrines In which of the above rows is the given information correctly matched?
questions.e: Inamgaon in Maharashtra is Chalcolithic and Mangadu in Kerala megalithic. Chandraketugarh is in West Bengal, and Salihundam is a Buddhist stupa complex, not rock-cut caves.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q55

questions.q: Who of the following rulers of medieval India gave permission to the Portuguese to build a fort at Bhatkal?
questions.e: Krishnadevaraya of Vijayanagara allowed the Portuguese to build a fort at Bhatkal.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q56

questions.q:
With reference to revenue collection by Cornwallis, consider the following statements:
1. Under the Ryotwari Settlement of revenue collection, the peasants were exempted from revenue payment in case of bad harvests or natural calamities.
2. Under the Permanent Settlement in Bengal, if the Zamindar failed to pay his revenues to the state, on or before the fixed date, he would be removed from his Zamindari.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: UPSC dropped this question. Under the Permanent Settlement a zamindar who missed the payment date lost his estate; ryotwari gave no exemption for bad harvests.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q57

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. There are no parables in Upanishads.
2. Upanishads were composed earlier than the Puranas.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The Upanishads contain parables, such as Shvetaketu and his father, and they predate the Puranas. Only 2 is correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q58

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. India is a member of the International Grains Council.
2. A country needs to be a member of the International Grains Council for exporting or importing rice and wheat.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: India is a member of the International Grains Council, but membership is not needed to trade rice or wheat.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q59

questions.q: Which one of the following was the latest inclusion in the Intangible Cultural Heritage List of UNESCO?
questions.e: Garba was inscribed in December 2023, after Chhau (2010), Kumbh Mela (2017) and Durga Puja (2021).
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q60

questions.q: Who was the Provisional President of the Constituent Assembly before Dr. Rajendra Prasad took over?
questions.e: Sachchidananda Sinha, the oldest member, was provisional President of the Constituent Assembly before Rajendra Prasad was elected.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q61

questions.q:
With reference to the Government of India Act, 1935, consider the following statements:
1. It provided for the establishment of an All India Federation based on the union of the British Indian Provinces and Princely States.
2. Defence and Foreign Affairs were kept under the control of the federal legislature.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The 1935 Act proposed an All-India Federation of provinces and princely states. Defence and foreign affairs were reserved for the Governor-General, not the federal legislature.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q62

questions.q: Which one of the following is a work attributed to playwright Bhasa?
questions.e: Madhyama-vyayoga is one of Bhasa's plays. Natyashastra is Bharata's treatise and Mahabhashya Patanjali's work on grammar.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q63

questions.q: Sanghabhuti, an Indian Buddhist monk, who travelled to China at the end of the fourth century AD, was the author of a commentary on:
questions.e: Sanghabhuti, a monk who went to China in the late 4th century, wrote a commentary on the Sarvastivada Vinaya.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q64

questions.q:
Consider the following properties included in the World Heritage List released by UNESCO:
1. Shantiniketan
2. Rani-ki-Vav
3. Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas
4. Mahabodhi Temple Complex at Bodhgaya
How many of the above properties were included in 2023?
questions.e: Santiniketan and the Hoysala temples were inscribed in 2023. Rani-ki-Vav was listed in 2014 and Mahabodhi in 2002.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q65

questions.q:
As per Article 368 of the Constitution of India, the Parliament may amend any provision of the Constitution by way of:
1. Addition
2. Variation
3. Repeal
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Article 368(1) lets Parliament amend any provision by way of addition, variation or repeal.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q66

questions.q:
Consider the following countries:
1. Italy
2. Japan
3. Nigeria
4. South Korea
5. South Africa
Which of the above countries are frequently mentioned in the media for their low birth rates, or ageing population or declining population?
questions.e: Italy, Japan and South Korea are known for low birth rates and ageing populations. Nigeria and South Africa have young, growing populations.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q67

questions.q:
Which of the following statements are correct in respect of a Money Bill in the Parliament?
1. Article 109 mentions special procedure in respect of Money Bills.
2. A Money Bill shall not be introduced in the Council of States.
3. The Rajya Sabha can either approve the Bill or suggest changes but cannot reject it.
4. Amendments to a Money Bill suggested by the Rajya Sabha have to be accepted by the Lok Sabha.
Select the answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Article 109 lays down the special procedure: Money Bills cannot start in the Rajya Sabha, which can only recommend changes within 14 days. The Lok Sabha may reject those recommendations.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q68

questions.q:
Which of the following is/are correctly matched in terms of equivalent rank in the three services of Indian Defence forces? Army Airforce Navy
1. Brigadier Air Commodore Commander
2. Major General Air Vice Marshal Vice Admiral
3. Major Squadron Leader Lieutenant Commander
4. Lieutenant Colonel Group Captain Captain
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: A Major equals a Squadron Leader and a Lieutenant Commander. The other rows misplace the Navy ranks.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q69

questions.q:
The North Eastern Council (NEC) was established by the North Eastern Council Act, 1971. Subsequent to the amendment of NEC Act in 2002, the Council comprises which of the following members?
1. Governor of the Constituent State
2. Chief Minister of the Constituent State
3. Three Members to be nominated by the President of India
4. The Home Minister of India
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: After the 2002 amendment, the NEC has the Governors and Chief Ministers of the eight states plus three members nominated by the President.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q70

questions.q: How many Delimitation Commissions have been constituted by the Government of India till December 2023?
questions.e: Delimitation Commissions were set up in 1952, 1963, 1973 and 2002: four.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q71

questions.q:
The Constitution (71st Amendment) Act, 1992 amends the Eighth Schedule to the Constitution to include which of the following languages?
1. Konkani
2. Manipuri
3. Nepali
4. Maithili
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: The 71st Amendment (1992) added Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali. Maithili came with the 92nd Amendment (2003).
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q72

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs: Party Its Leader
1. Bharatiya Jana Sangh Dr. Shyama Prasad Mukherjee
2. Socialist Party
C. Rajagopalachari
3. Congress for Democracy Jagjivan Ram
4. Swatantra Party Acharya Narendra Dev
How many of the above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Syama Prasad Mookerjee founded the Jana Sangh and Jagjivan Ram led the Congress for Democracy. Rajagopalachari led the Swatantra Party, and Narendra Dev was a socialist.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q73

questions.q:
Which of the following statements are correct about the Constitution of India?
1. Powers of the Municipalities are given in Part IX A of the Constitution.
2. Emergency provisions are given in Part XVIII of the Constitution.
3. Provisions related to the amendment of the Constitution are given in Part XX of the Constitution.
Select the answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Part IXA covers Municipalities, Part XVIII Emergency provisions and Part XX amendment. All three are correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q74

questions.q: Which one of the following statements is correct as per the Constitution of India?
o: Inter-State trade and commerce is a State subject under the State List.
Inter-State migration is a State subject under the State List.
Inter-State quarantine is a Union subject under the Union List.
Corporation tax is a State subject under the State List.
questions.e: Inter-State quarantine (with inter-State migration) is Entry 81 of the Union List. Inter-State trade and corporation tax are also Union subjects.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q75

questions.q: Under which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India, has the Supreme Court of India placed the Right to Privacy?
questions.e: The Puttaswamy judgment (2017) placed the right to privacy under Article 21.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q76

questions.q:
What are the duties of the Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) as Head of the Department of Military Affairs?
1. Permanent Chairman of Chiefs of Staff Committee
2. Exercise military command over the three Service Chiefs
3. Principal Military Advisor to Defence Minister on all tri-Service matters
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: The CDS is permanent Chairman of the Chiefs of Staff Committee and principal military adviser to the Defence Minister. He does not command the three Service Chiefs.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q77

questions.q: Operations undertaken by the Army towards upliftment of the local population in remote areas to include addressing of their basic needs is called:
questions.e: Operation Sadbhavana is the Army's civic action programme in remote border areas.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q78

questions.q: The longest border between any two countries in the world is between:
o: Canada and the United States of America
questions.e: Canada and the USA share the world's longest border, about 8,891 km.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q79

questions.q:
Which of the following statements about the Ethics Committee in the Lok Sabha are correct?
1. Initially it was an ad-hoc Committee.
2. Only a Member of the Lok Sabha can make a complaint relating to unethical conduct of a member of the Lok Sabha.
3. This Committee cannot take up any matter which is sub-judice.
Select the answer using the code given below:
questions.e: The Ethics Committee began as an ad hoc committee and does not take up sub judice matters. Complaints can come from any person through a Member, so 2 is wrong.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q80

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding ‘Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam’:
1. Provisions will come into effect from the 18th Lok Sabha.
2. This will be in force for 15 years after becoming an Act.
3. There are provisions for the reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes Women within the quota reserved for the Scheduled Castes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The women's reservation Act lasts 15 years and reserves one-third of SC seats for SC women. It takes effect after the next census and delimitation, not from the 18th Lok Sabha.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q81

questions.q:
Which of the following statements about 'Exercise Mitra Shakti-2023' are correct?
1. This was a joint military exercise between India and Bangladesh.
2. It commenced in Aundh (Pune).
3. Joint response during counter-terrorism operations was a goal of this operation.
4. Indian Air Force was a part of this exercise.
Select the answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Mitra Shakti 2023 was held at Aundh (Pune), focused on counter-terrorism and included the IAF. It was with Sri Lanka, not Bangladesh.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q82

questions.q: A Writ of Prohibition is an order issued by the Supreme Court or High Courts to:
o: a government officer prohibiting him from taking a particular action.
the Parliament/Legislative Assembly to pass a law on Prohibition.
the lower court prohibiting continuation of proceedings in a case.
the Government prohibiting it from following an unconstitutional policy.
questions.e: A writ of prohibition stops a lower court from continuing a case beyond its jurisdiction.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q83
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. It is the Governor of the State who recognizes and declares any community of that State as a Scheduled Tribe.
2. A community declared as a Scheduled Tribe in a State need not be so in another State.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The President, not the Governor, notifies Scheduled Tribes (Article 342), and the list is State-specific.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q84

questions.q:
With reference to Union Budget, consider the following statements:
1. The Union Finance Minister on behalf of the Prime Minister lays the Annual Financial Statement before both the Houses of Parliament.
2. At the Union level, no demand for a grant can be made except on the recommendation of the President of India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The Finance Minister lays the Annual Financial Statement on the President's behalf, and no demand for grant can be made except on the President's recommendation (Article 113). UPSC's key counts both as correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q85

questions.q: Who of the following is the author of the books "The India Way" and "Why Bharat Matters"?
questions.e: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar wrote 'The India Way' (2020) and 'Why Bharat Matters' (2024).
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q86

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs: Country Reason for being in the news
1. Argentina Worst economic crisis
2. Sudan War between the country's regular army and paramilitary forces
3. Turkey Rescinded its membership of NATO
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Argentina faced a severe economic crisis and Sudan a war between the army and the RSF. Turkey remains a NATO member.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q87

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Sumed pipeline is a strategic route for Persian Gulf oil and natural gas shipments to Europe.
Statement-II: Sumed pipeline connects the Red Sea with the Mediterranean Sea.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The SUMED pipeline across Egypt links the Red Sea with the Mediterranean, which makes it a route for Gulf oil to Europe. II explains I.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q88

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Red Sea receives very little precipitation in any form.
2. No water enters the Red Sea from rivers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The Red Sea lies in an arid region with scant rain and no river inflow. Both are correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q89

questions.q: According to the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), which one of the following is the largest source of sulphur dioxide emissions?
questions.e: According to the US EPA, fossil fuel power plants are the largest source of SO₂.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q90

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: There is instability and worsening security situation in the Sahel region.
Statement-II: There have been military takeovers/coups d'état in several countries of the Sahel region in the recent past.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Security in the Sahel has worsened, and repeated coups in Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger have contributed. II explains I.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q91

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: India does not import apples from the United States of America.
Statement-II: In India, the law prohibits the import of Genetically Modified food without the approval of the competent authority.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: India does import apples from the US. The FSS Act bars import of GM food without approval.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q92

questions.q:
With reference to the Speaker of the Lok Sabha, consider the following statements: While any resolution for the removal of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha is under consideration
1. He/She shall not preside.
2. He/She shall not have the right to speak.
3. He/She shall not be entitled to vote on the resolution in the first instance.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: During a removal resolution the Speaker cannot preside but may speak and vote in the first instance (Article 96).
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q93

questions.q:
With reference to the Indian Parliament, consider the following statements:
1. A bill pending in the Lok Sabha lapses on its dissolution.
2. A bill passed by the Lok Sabha and pending in the Rajya Sabha lapses on the dissolution of the Lok Sabha.
3. A bill in regard to which the President of India notified his/her intention to summon the Houses to a joint sitting lapses on the dissolution of the Lok Sabha.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Bills pending in the Lok Sabha, or passed by it and pending in the Rajya Sabha, lapse on dissolution. A bill for which a joint sitting has been notified does not lapse.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q94

questions.q:
With reference to the Parliament of India, consider the following statements:
1. Prorogation of a House by the President of India does not require the advice of the Council of Ministers.
2. Prorogation of a House is generally done after the House is adjourned sine die but there is no bar to the President of India prorogating the House which is in session.
3. Dissolution of the Lok Sabha is done by the President of India who, save in exceptional circumstances, does so on the advice of the Council of Ministers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The President prorogues and dissolves on the Council of Ministers' advice, so 1 is wrong. Prorogation can occur even while a House is in session.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q95

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The European Parliament approved The Net-Zero Industry Act recently.
Statement-II: The European Union intends to achieve carbon neutrality by 2040 and therefore aims to develop all of its own clean technology by that time.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The European Parliament approved the Net-Zero Industry Act in 2024. The EU target is net zero by 2050, and the Act aims for 40% domestic clean-tech production, not all of it.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q96

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Recently, Venezuela has achieved a rapid recovery from its economic crisis and succeeded in preventing its people from fleeing/emigrating to other countries.
Statement-II: Venezuela has the world's largest oil reserves.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Venezuela has not recovered and millions have emigrated. It does have the world's largest proven oil reserves.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q97

questions.q:
With reference to the Digital India Land Records Modernisation Programme, consider the following statements:
1. To implement the scheme, the Central Government provides 100% funding.
2. Under the Scheme, Cadastral Maps are digitised.
3. An initiative has been undertaken to transliterate the Records of Rights from local language to any of the languages recognized by the Constitution of India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: DILRMP is fully centrally funded, digitises cadastral maps and transliterates land records into scheduled languages. All three are correct.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q98

questions.q:
With reference to the ‘Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan’, consider the following statements:
1. This scheme guarantees a minimum package of antenatal care services to women in their second and third trimesters of pregnancy and six months post-delivery health care service in any government health facility.
2. Under this scheme, private sector health care providers of certain specialities can volunteer to provide services at nearby government health facilities.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: PMSMA provides antenatal care on the 9th of every month and invites private doctors to volunteer. It has no six-month post-delivery package.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q99

questions.q:
With reference to the Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-dhan (PM-SYM) Yojana, consider the following statements:
1. The entry age group for enrolment in the scheme is 21 to 40 years.
2. Age specific contribution shall be made by the beneficiary.
3. Each subscriber under the scheme shall receive a minimum pension of ₹ 3,000 per month after attaining the age of 60 years.
4. Family pension is applicable to the spouse and unmarried daughters.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: PM-SYM requires age-specific contributions and assures ₹3,000 a month from 60. Entry age is 18-40, and family pension goes only to the spouse.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2024, GS Paper I, Q100
